segments.title: 第200章 寒假的安排
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Era Chapter 200: Arrangements for Winter Break

After delivering the scarf, Li Luo went back to writing.

Yan Zhusheng didn't go out. She sat obediently on the edge of the bed, watching him write, but she didn't peek at the specific content.

After all, Li Luo had said before that if someone was looking over his shoulder at what he was writing, he wouldn't be able to write.

Around six in the evening, Li Luo stopped tapping the keyboard and stretched in his seat.

"Let's go, to school."

"Okay."

The two of them walked out of the bedroom, called for Xu Youyu who was in the study, and then headed to the First Affiliated High School together.

On the way, Yan Zhusheng asked curiously, "Li Luo, are you still making egg-fried rice tonight?"

"No." Li Luo shook his head. "Selling egg-fried rice was just a way to save money for Zhao Rongjun. Now that he's bought the down jackets for his grandparents, there's no need to go to all that trouble anymore."

"Oh, okay."

"Are you craving it?" Li Luo asked with a chuckle. "If you really want some, I can make a separate portion for you tonight and deliver it."

"Then never mind, I don't want it that much," Yan Zhusheng said, shaking her head.

"Actually, if Zhusheng wants to eat it, you could just apply to be a day student next semester," Xu Youyu chimed in from the side, smiling persuasively. "Don't we still have a spare room? You can just rent it, and you'll even earn Li Luo some rent money."

Hearing this, Yan Zhusheng was a little tempted and couldn't help but look at Li Luo.

"It's not that simple to decide something like this." Li Luo looked exasperated. "At the very least, you have to ask for your mom's opinion, right?"

The three of them chatted idly like this and soon arrived at the First Affiliated High School.

Xu Youyu bid them a temporary farewell on the first floor and headed toward the tenth-grade building, while Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng went upstairs to the classroom of Class Eight to attend the Sunday evening self-study session.

Li Luo had originally thought this ordinary day would just pass like this.

But when the first period ended, Zhao Rongjun came sauntering down from upstairs, secretly sought out Li Luo, and asked in a low voice, "Are we really not doing it anymore?"

"We're really not." Seeing the guy's eager look, Li Luo was at a loss for whether to laugh or cry. "I'm finding that you quite enjoy hardship?"

"What's so hard about it?" Zhao Rongjun shook his head repeatedly. "I don't feel like it's hard at all, and it's a lot of fun."

Seeing Zhao Rongjun's current state, Li Luo couldn't help but think of a joke he had seen in his previous life.

It was about a poor student who didn't study well, so his family arranged for him to move bricks on a construction site, hoping he would realize how hard life was after entering society and would then have a change of heart and study properly.

But when the guy got to the construction site, he worked with incredible enthusiasm. He moved bricks every day, earning two to three hundred yuan, ate heartily, and no longer suffered from insomnia.

Wasn't this much better than idling away his days at school?

So his family couldn't drag him back even if they tried; he was dead set on continuing to work at the construction site.

Although Zhao Rongjun hadn't reached that point, it was quite similar.

After all, students had been supported by their parents since they were young.

The advantage was not having to worry too much about money, having food to eat and clothes to wear; children didn't have to think about these things themselves.

But at the same time, the money they could control themselves was also limited. After starting school, they often only had some living expenses, all of which were charged to their school meal cards.

They barely had any pocket money.

Under such circumstances, if you told a student that by working just over an hour more each night, he could get fifty or sixty yuan in pocket money...

Probably quite a few would happily tag along.

In fact, some quick-witted students, though perhaps average academically, had already started their own businesses at school on the sly.

Things like fetching breakfast, helping with homework, renting out cell phones, and so on, for a few yuan each time. Although it wasn't much, they at least already had this kind of money-making mindset.

After entering society, this type of student might fare a bit better than those who only knew how to bury their noses in books.

However, Zhao Rongjun was a future Qianjiang University prospect. After graduating and working hard for a couple more years, he would be making over ten thousand a month no matter what.

Li Luo still didn't really want to hold this kid back.

"The final exams are almost here, you should focus." Li Luo shook his head helplessly. "And did you forget last time? That supermarket owner already came over to question us."

"If people find out we're doing this all the time and it affects the supermarket's business, they will definitely call security to stop us in the future."

"After all, we know our ingredients are safe, but the school doesn't. To prevent any food safety issues, they definitely won't allow students to eat things from outside."

"If you get caught, you might even get a lecture from the teacher."

After hearing Li Luo's analysis, Zhao Rongjun's head drooped in disappointment, and he temporarily gave up on the idea.

"Oh, right." Seeing him like this, Li Luo immediately changed the subject. "After you went home yesterday, did you give the down jackets to your grandparents? What did they say?"

"That." The moment this was brought up, Zhao Rongjun's face lit up again. He chuckled and scratched his head. "My grandparents were so happy. They kept saying they felt bad about the money and even asked if I could return them."

"I purposely said I couldn't, and if they didn't want them, I could only throw them away."

"Then they had no choice but to accept them."

"But after dinner, the two of them immediately put on the new clothes and went to the small park next door for a walk to show them off to the other old grandpas and grandmas."

"My dad heard about it from my grandpa and even came over specially this afternoon to give me a hundred yuan in pocket money."

Zhao Rongjun smiled foolishly, clearly having tasted the sweetness of being filial to his elders. It wasn't just the monetary reward, but more of a spiritual enjoyment that made him very happy.

Seeing him like this, Li Luo also smiled in gratification. In fact, it wasn't just Zhao Rongjun; it was Li Luo himself too.

Although he had consciously been better to his parents after being reborn, and had even been helping out at the breakfast stall since the high school entrance exams, if it weren't for Zhao Rongjun's reminder, Li Luo wouldn't have known when he would have thought to buy his parents new clothes.

"Alright, just focus on reviewing for now. Getting a good score on the final exams is much better than earning that bit of pocket money," Li Luo said, patting Zhao Rongjun's shoulder.

Soon, the bell for the second period of evening self-study rang.

Zhao Rongjun hurried back to his classroom.

Li Luo returned to his seat and continued to study.

With about ten minutes left before the end of class, Yan Zhusheng poked Li Luo's arm at the right moment, then got up and walked out.

Seeing this, Li Luo tidied up his desk and schoolbag, then followed her out of the classroom. He went to the sports field opposite the school building and found Yan Zhusheng waiting there.

The two had already grown accustomed to their night runs. They walked onto the track with ease, not needing to say a word to each other.

Yan Zhusheng had already skillfully put his earphones in for him. Then the two of them started running, both familiar with each other's pace, and began to run with even breaths.

After finishing four laps, the two gradually slowed down. They glanced at the time; there was still a while before class ended, so they started to walk around the sports field.

"Li Luo, do you have any plans for winter break?" Yan Zhusheng untied the scarf from her neck to get some air and asked Li Luo.

"Not really," Li Luo thought for a moment. "I used up a lot of my manuscript stockpile before, so I have to replenish it."

"Oh, right." Li Luo suddenly remembered something and said to Yan Zhusheng, "From February 6th to the 9th, I'll probably have to go to the city for a few days to attend some writer's association symposium or something."

"Oh," Yan Zhusheng nodded.

"Why are you suddenly asking about winter break?"

"Just asking." Yan Zhusheng walked on her tiptoes for a few steps before saying, "After winter break starts at the end of the month, I'll probably have to accompany my mom abroad for a follow-up checkup. I'll have to rush back around New Year's Eve."

"Is that so?" Li Luo's expression became thoughtful. "Are you getting a check-up too?"

"Hmm?" Yan Zhusheng looked at him strangely. "What check-up would I get?"

"Uh... just a physical," Li Luo said. "Although we're still young and relatively healthy, it's not a bad thing to have a routine check-up every year."

"Oh, I see," Yan Zhusheng nodded and agreed. "Then I'll get a physical."

Hearing her reply, Li Luo breathed a small sigh of relief.

However, a heart condition might not necessarily be detectable now.

After all, in his previous life, Yan Zhusheng hadn't been diagnosed with a heart condition until she was in her thirties.

At this age, there might not be any signs yet.

But if they could find something and take preventive measures in advance, that would certainly be for the best.

The two of them had more or less finished their chat. With about two minutes left before class ended, they returned to the classroom together.

After the dismissal bell rang, Li Luo waited in the classroom for Ying Chanxi. They went downstairs together, met up with Xu Youyu, and headed home.

Having just been asked by Yan Zhusheng about his winter break plans, Li Luo couldn't help but worry about the symposium.

After all, he had to go to the city for three days. If Ying Chanxi looked for him during that time, it would be quite easy for his secret to be exposed.

So Li Luo asked Ying Chanxi, "Do you have any plans for winter break?"

"Plans?" Ying Chanxi blinked, thinking for a moment. "I don't really have any plans. I'll just be at home during winter break. Oh, right."

"Hmm? What's up?" Li Luo pressed.

"Isn't break starting at the end of the month?" Ying Chanxi said. "My dad said he might go abroad for a business trip in early February and asked if I wanted to go with him. He said he won't be too busy over there and should have time to show me around. I'm still considering it."

"There's that?" Li Luo raised his eyebrows.

In his previous life, he had a falling out with Ying Chanxi after the high school entrance exams, so he didn't know about her winter break plans.

But after a quick search in his memory palace, he did indeed find a memory of his parents mentioning Ying Zhicheng's affairs at the New Year's dinner table, saying that he had gone abroad for a while.

"Then you should probably go, right?" Li Luo said. "After all, you and Uncle Ying don't see each other often. It's a rare opportunity to travel together."

"Mmm..." Ying Chanxi was also in a bit of a dilemma. She touched the light red scarf around her neck and looked at Li Luo. "Do you want me to go?"

"...You have to decide something like this for yourself. Why are you asking me?"

"What if I'm gone for many days and you miss me?" Ying Chanxi said with a huff.

"Don't worry, I won't."

"You!" Ying Chanxi was angered by him. She stomped her foot and said, "And I promised Auntie Lin I would keep an eye on you. What if you run around all over the place during winter break?"

"You sure worry a lot." Li Luo shook his head helplessly, pressed down on her head, and ruffled her hair. "Just go and have fun. I've never even been abroad. Take lots of pictures when you go and broaden my horizons too."

"Don't worry, Xixi," Xu Youyu giggled from the side. "I'll keep an eye on him for you. If he dares to run around, I'll report him to you."

"Senior, I'll be back home for the break. How can you still keep an eye on me?" Li Luo said, rolling his eyes.

"Then remember to help out more at the breakfast stall," Ying Chanxi reminded him. "Uncle and Auntie work very hard. Since you're on break, you should help out more."

"Got it," Li Luo nodded. "So did Uncle Ying say how long he'll be gone?"

"I think about half a month," Ying Chanxi recalled. "Anyway, he'll definitely be back before New Year's Eve."

(End of Chapter)
